prologue-title-0: What does it take to emulate just one neuron?
prologue-body-0: Before we try to emulate the entire nervous system, let's just try to understand how we can model a singular neuron & its dynamics.
prologue-title-1: Just knowing the shape/morphology isn't enough.
prologue-body-1: A reconstruction tells us where the branches go, but doesn’t tell us how the membrane responds, which channels are active, or when this cell will fire.
prologue-body-2: We can first give a cell a known input and measure its response. If a model can reproduce these dynamics, we've gotten much closer to simulation. In this explainable, we're going to try to build that!
recording-introduction: There have been a ton of experiments on single-neuron current injections and resultant voltage recording. As you can see in the graph, the we get an 'action potential' (or spike) as a response. This is our starting point!
lesson-1: What exactly are we trying to reproduce?
lesson-2: Here, emulating means building a model that predicts a chosen response to an input + predict forward in time given a current state. A big part of modeling complex systems is deciding what types of data to keep, determining parameters, and using modeling equations through time... and comparing this with biological results.  A useful model might predict when a neuron fires without reproducing every detail inside it.
lesson-3: That leaves a tradeoff: more mechanisms mean more quantities to estimate and update, maybe requiring more compute or data that is impossible to collect at scale. A simpler model costs less to run, but can leave out a behavior we care about and not give us a 'real' emulation. The experiment decides whether those omissions matter.
